questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language and the possibility to follow courses relevant to my degree at home. I wanted to practice my english in both speaking and writing. Doing a semester abroad allowed me to work with law in depth in english both in terms of everyday language as well as professional.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy getting information upon arrival. The introduction held by the University was good, but I do with they would have made a group for getting in touch with the other exchange students as it would have made it easier getting in touch with people doing the same courses as you as well as exchanging practical information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They did two different welcomes. One of them was for all international students, which was not that good. The other was only for the people doing exchange. This was good, I wished we'd have a bit more like that. We also did a tour of campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was alright. I just googled student accommodations in the city. I also looked at airbnb and different kinds of housing, but had a hard time figuring out where to live, as you just don't know the city before you get there. I chose student accommodation close to campus, which was quite expensive to live in but I am happy with my choice. The other students living in different student accommodations said my building was by far the best even though a bit more expensive than the other options. I lived at the Switch in Adelaide.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I chose accommodation only about 150 meters from campus so a bit hard to say as I felt like I was almost on campus. I am happy that I lived in the CBD and close to campus. I think if I didn't live close to campus I would've chosen something closer to the beach. But I think staying close to campus is important to be able to do impulsive stuff with the other exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think in general the process of registration and everything else regarding the exchange has been a bit difficult. I think there's a lot of different things and deadlines to be aware of and I'd wish there was a better way to get an overview of what you need to fill out and when etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I needed to fill out a lot of boxes and questions and apply for the different courses in three different programs and websites. I had then got my courses approved manually of by the university as we couldn't put in the requisites for the courses. After approval and the start of the semester they wrote back to me that I could in fact not take those courses together so I had to go through the process again and they had to manually confirm again, and by then a lot of the courses where not available anymore

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a "hotline" for help at the university and an email you could write to

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took some attemps as answered above

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would make sure to apply for the courses early on and check with the university that you're allowed to follow chosen courses at the same time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took some courses that were more introductory as the law system is completely different to ours. Further I took some classes of criminology as the theories can be applied better to the danish law system.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar to the way of teaching of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Explaining Crime and Deviance
Policing and Crime Control
Introduction to Law
Environmental Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Explaining Crime and Deviance and Policing and Crime Control as the theories can be used internationally. Further, Introduction to Law teaches you a lot by the Australian common law system as well as the history and society of Australia, which I think is a very important part of exchange.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to extend my visa because I stayed an extra month. This costs 2.500,00 kr. as well as you'd be applying from Australia

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive. Other than that I think in general the prices are pretty much what you'd spend in Denmark, going out to eat and experiences costs about the same as in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different clubs were available both cultural and sports and more. I joind the sailing club for a bit. A lot of others did painting and soccer and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There's a few activities planned for exchange students only, which I would recommend going to.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think the nature around Adelaide is amazing. Explore the beaches and the hills, go to Hahndorf, visit the wineries, loads of good restaurants and walks to do in the area. If you go to the national parks you'll most definitely see both koalas and kangaroos

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture is very laidback and very easy. It's very western so adjusting was easy. Only thing is that Australia is very much a morning country and everything closes quite early, which you need to get used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of international students from Asia. I lived with two very sweet girls from Sri Lanka, but heard a lot of stories from other exchange students who lived with others who had a very different culture from them, which could be a bit challenging when sharing a space.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid back and friendliness of the people. Everyone is so open and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Most importantly to look forward and enjoy the experience. But to make sure that the courses are confirmed in their combination as well and to join a university club

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The memories and friendships I've made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being aware from home was sometimes difficult. But the university is good at wording that this is completely normal and have made arrangements that are easily in reach if you need someone to talk to

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
